nodes.natural_language: Given the system x+y+z=a, x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}=b^{2}, xy=z^{2} with a,b constants, find conditions on a,b such that solutions x,y,z are distinct positive reals.
nodes.statement: ∃ distinct x,y,z>0 satisfying the system ⇔ a,b satisfy the required inequalities derived from Vieta and positivity constraints

nodes.natural_language: Restate the theorem as the target claim to prove: the system admits distinct positive solutions x,y,z precisely when a,b meet the derived conditions.
nodes.statement: The solutions x,y,z are distinct positive numbers if and only if a>0, b^{2}>(2a^{2})/3 and a^{3}-3ab^{2}+2a^{3}/27>0 (or equivalent simplified inequalities).

nodes.natural_language: From (x+y+z)^2 = x^2+y^2+z^2 + 2(xy+yz+zx) we obtain a^2 = b^2 + 2(xy + z(x+y)).
Substituting xy=z^{2} and x+y=a-z into the identity a^{2}=b^{2}+2(xy+z(x+y)) yields a^{2}=b^{2}+2az.

Hence z=(a^{2}-b^{2})/(2a) whenever a
eq0.
x and y are roots of the quadratic equation t^{2} - (a - z)t + z^{2} = 0.
nodes.statement: x,y are roots of t^{2} - (a-z)t + z^{2} = 0

nodes.natural_language: For x,y to be distinct positive reals, the discriminant D = (a-z)^{2} - 4z^{2} must be positive, and both roots positive (sum a-z>0, product z^{2}>0).
nodes.statement: D=(a-z)^{2}-4z^{2}>0 and a-z>0, z>0 for distinct positive x,y

nodes.natural_language: x and y are the two roots of the quadratic t^{2}-(a-z)t+z^{2}=0.
nodes.statement: x,y are roots of t^{2} - (a-z)t + z^{2} = 0

nodes.natural_language: For x,y to be real and distinct the discriminant (a-z)^{2}-4z^{2} must be positive.
The discriminant of the quadratic is (a-z)^2-4z^2=(a-3z)(a+z).
x and y are real and distinct iff (a-3z)(a+z)>0.
nodes.statement: x,y real and distinct ⇔ (a-3z)(a+z)>0

nodes.natural_language: Then x and y are the two roots of the quadratic t^{2}-(a-z)t+z^{2}=0.
nodes.statement: x,y are roots of t^{2} - (a-z)t + z^{2} = 0

nodes.natural_language: The discriminant of this quadratic is D=(a-z)^{2}-4z^{2}, so x and y are real and distinct if and only if D>0.
nodes.statement: x,y real and distinct \Leftrightarrow D=(a-z)^{2}-4z^{2}>0

nodes.natural_language: Require z>0 together with a-z>0 and D=(a-3z)(a+z)>0; substituting z=(a^{2}-b^{2})/(2a) produces the explicit inequalities a>0, b^{2}>(2a^{2})/3 and a^{3}-3ab^{2}+2a^{3}/27>0.
nodes.statement: z>0 \wedge a-z>0 \wedge (a-3z)(a+z)>0 \Leftrightarrow a>0, b^{2}>(2a^{2})/3, a^{3}-3ab^{2}+2a^{3}/27>0

nodes.natural_language: The system admits distinct positive solutions x,y,z precisely when a>0, b^{2}>(2a^{2})/3 and a^{3}-3ab^{2}+2a^{3}/27>0.
nodes.statement: distinct positive x,y,z exist ⇔ a>0 ∧ b^{2}>(2a^{2})/3 ∧ a^{3}-3ab^{2}+2a^{3}/27>0

nodes.natural_language: For x,y real and distinct we need D>0, i.e. (a-3z)(a+z)>0.
nodes.statement: x,y real and distinct ⇒ D>0 ⇒ (a-3z)(a+z)>0

nodes.natural_language: x,y>0 also requires a-z>0 (hence a+z>0 automatically if z>0).
nodes.statement: x,y>0 \Rightarrow a-z>0 (and a+z>0 follows from z>0)

nodes.natural_language: The system admits distinct positive solutions x,y,z precisely when a>0, b^{2}>(2a^{2})/3 and a^{3}-3ab^{2}+2a^{3}/27>0.
nodes.statement: distinct positive x,y,z exist ⇔ a>0 ∧ b^{2}>(2a^{2})/3 ∧ a^{3}-3ab^{2}+2a^{3}/27>0

nodes.natural_language: z>0 together with a-z>0 (hence a>0) is necessary and sufficient for both roots x,y to be positive
nodes.statement: z>0 \wedge (a-z)>0 \Leftrightarrow x>0 \wedge y>0

nodes.natural_language: The system admits distinct positive solutions x,y,z precisely when a>0, b^{2}>(2a^{2})/3 and a^{3}-3ab^{2}+2a^{3}/27>0.
